The test image shows a soybean leaf with a large irregular necrotic lesion — tan/brown center with a yellowish-green border/halo around it. The lesion is water-soaked looking and spans across a broad section of the leaf. Key candidates: Bacterial_Blight (angular, water-soaked lesions with yellow halos), Phytophthora, or Downy_mildew.

Now I'll view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates before deciding.
This Bacterial_Blight reference shows many small angular yellow lesions scattered on leaves — not the same as the single large necrotic lesion in the test image. Let me check Phytophthora.
Phytophthora shows whole-plant wilting — not matching. Let me check Anthracnose and Downy_mildew.
Anthracnose shows stem symptoms — not matching. Let me check Cercospora as my 4th candidate.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Single large, irregular tan/brown necrotic lesion spanning much of the leaf, with a distinct yellowish-green margin/halo. The lesion has somewhat angular edges following leaf structure, with a water-soaked appearance at margins.

- **Bacterial_Blight** (ref): Showed early-stage small angular yellow lesions — this matches the same disease at a more advanced/coalesced stage where lesions merge into a large necrotic area. The yellow-green halo is the key diagnostic feature.
- **Phytophthora** (ref): Whole-plant wilting — no match.
- **Anthracnose** (ref): Stem browning — no match.
- **Cercospora** (ref): Many small purple-brown spots scattered — no match.

The large coalesced necrotic lesion with angular margin and distinct yellowish-green halo is characteristic of advanced Bacterial_Blight on soybean leaves.
